title: Jones wants to cover the unrecorded years 1926 to 1936
summary: Jones mentions his unpublished writing and complains that histories begin with him joining Basie, skipping the years from 1926 to 1936.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: What I would like to do is things that I - have about three sections of articles and things - I've thrown away a lot of things and I dedicated in from the very beginning to what I would do. I wrote a thing in the articles and things that I have that hasn't been published, "Peoples I've Met". I cover the 48 states and I would like to make a jump from where we are now to start in the year 1930, which would be important.

We got lot's of time to do that, Jo, and it's important - one of the stipulations that I have in the interview is that (I can read it to you) you should get the background, you know, the early background, so that after I work into that with you I'm just going to let
you talk about whatever you want to talk about.

...You must remember this, Milt, that all the books that have ever been written about various musicians, they start with me, I joined Count Basie in 1935. He joined Count Basie in 1936. That sounds like I was just born, like Topsy. But what about the years from '26 to '36?
That's what we're trying to cover now.
This's where we're getting to. From the year '26 we go professionally - and I can start with you very vividly -
